mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of the triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in Real Final Sales of Domestic Product (RSAFS) by more than 1% month-over-month signals weakening consumer demand, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations decline.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of the triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between RSAFS drops and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% over three months signals labor market weakness, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as it indicates a broader economic slowdown.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of the triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in Industrial Production Index (INDPRO) by more than 2% over three months signals strengthening supply-side fundamentals, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as it indicates robust economic activity.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of the triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the correlation between INDPRO increases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% month-over-month, it signals inflationary pressure, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate tighter monetary policy.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 70% of the triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between CPIAUCSL increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An always-on signal where a low Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) below 2% indicates accommodative monetary policy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as liquidity is abundant and borrowing costs are low.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances when FEDFUNDS is below 2%, or if the correlation between low FEDFUNDS and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month, it signals a tight labor market with strong job growth, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending power increases.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the joint effect of UNRATE and PAYEMS on returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) decline by more than 10% year-over-year and the Real Final Sales of Domestic Product (RSAFS) also decline by more than 1% month-over-month, it signals a significant weakening in both housing and consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as economic activity slows.
candidate_trigger: HOUST declines > 10% YoY and RSAFS declines > 1% MoM
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of the triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the joint effect of HOUST and RSAFS declines on returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
